Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
- What the test expects
  - The regression test exercises Beider-Morse Phonetic Matching (BMPM) in APPROX mode with nameType=GENERIC and concat=true, asserting that encoding "Bendzin" yields the five tokens: bndzn|bntsn|bnzn|vndzn|vntsn.

- How the code processes the input
  - PhoneticEngine.encode(String) lowers the input and delegates to encode(input, languageSet).
  - In encode(input, languageSet), rules are loaded (core rules plus final “common” and language-specific rules), input is normalized, and because concat=true it proceeds with the single word unchanged.
  - It builds phonemes by scanning the input with RulesApplication, then applies two passes of “final rules”: first common (finalRules1), then language-specific (finalRules2), returning the string from the resulting PhonemeBuilder.

- Where things go wrong
  - In applyFinalRules(PhonemeBuilder, Map<String, List<Rule>>), the method collects results into a TreeSet<Rule.Phoneme> with a comparator that orders by phoneme text only and ignores the language set.
  - The code comment explicitly notes this: the ordering ignores the language set; thus when adding new phonemes, equal texts with different language sets must be merged to avoid losing variants. However, the implementation simply does phonemes.addAll(subBuilder.getPhonemes()) and does not merge language sets for equal-text phonemes.
  - Consequence: Whenever multiple phonemes share the same text but originate from different languages, only one survives in the TreeSet and the others are dropped, losing the union of their language sets.

- Why that breaks this test
  - BMPM relies on language sets carried with each phoneme to control the second pass of language-specific final rules. For names like “Bendzin,” variants such as bndzn/bnzn/bntsn and vndzn/vntsn originate from different language pathways (e.g., Slavic/Germanic leading to different handling of b/v and dz/ts).
  - After the first final-rules pass, equal-text phonemes that should collectively carry a union of languages are collapsed to a single entry with a reduced language set. The subsequent language-specific pass therefore applies fewer (or different) transformations, producing an incorrect set of tokens compared to the original/expected behavior.
  - This precisely matches the bug report about “incorrect tokens” and the evolving BMPM algorithm: here the defect stems from implementation details, not rule content—loss of language information causes missing or altered variants, so the expected 5-token output is not produced.

In short, the failure is caused by applyFinalRules dropping language information for phonemes that share the same text, due to using a TreeSet comparator that ignores languages and not merging language sets for equal-text phonemes. This alters the language-specific final processing and yields the wrong token set for “Bendzin.”

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
